notes: Good early start: Window of Opportunity steals Tomorrow's Headline on T1, then Maintenance Access + Docklands Pass takes Freedom of Information on T8 and Tread Lightly takes Stoke the Embers on T9. From T12 to T18 it clicks for credits every turn up to 28 credits with Carmen and Tremolo installed and never pressures Server 4 or the centrals. It ended a turn tagged on T7 and lost two Daily Casts on T8.

It won by advancing Fujii Asset Retrieval (T2-T4), Project Yagi-Uda (T5-T7) and Sericulture Expansion (T9-T11) over several turns in a remote behind a single Tatu-Bola, against a Runner with 17-30 credits who only got lucky by not running. The Corp sat at 0-3 credits from T4 to T9, could not rez anything, and banked AU Co. counters until T11.

After breaking Ballista with Boi-tata on T4, from T5 to T20 it clicks for credits every turn, reaching 72 credits, and never makes a run. It let the Corp advance and score Divested Trust (T7, T13), Above the Law (T16, T21) and more out of Server 2 and Server 3 with no plan at all.

Ansel 1.0 on Server 1 (rezzed T1) locked out a broke Runner, which was strong, but it then spent 10 turns at 0-1 credits, drawing on T2-T4 instead of clicking for credits to advance faster. Architect Deployment Test only scored on T6 and Melies on T10, scoring slowly while the Runner was helpless.

The early HQ steals were good (Post-Truth Dividend and Freedom of Information on T2 via Docklands Pass). After that it repeatedly ran into known Piranhas on HQ with no breaker (T5, T7, T11-T14), losing a card each time, and into Doomscroll + N-Pot on Server 1 (T5, T8, T9, T15). The T9 Concerto run into Doomscroll with 2 tags cost three cards, and by T13-T15 it had 0 credits and kept bouncing off Ping.

It stacked three ice on an Otto Campaign remote (T3, T5, T6) while R&D and HQ had one ice each, so Architect Deployment Test, Megaprix Qualifier and two Project Ingatan were stolen from the centrals. On T7, with the Runner at 6 points, it spent all its clicks on draws and credits with 12 credits and Ansel 1.0 in hand instead of icing R&D, and lost that turn.

The early HQ steals of Remastered Edition and the Oracle Thinktank steal through Gauss on T9 were good. Later it reinstalled Daily Casts and then ran unpaid into F2P, which bounced Daily Casts or Unity back to the grip (T12, T14, T15). It also ran Archives repeatedly for little value and let Next Big Thing score on T14.

Aggressive multi-access through Hammer won the game, but it never built an economy after Buzzsaw was trashed T3 and spent T4-T8 at 0-2 credits paying to clear Hammer tags. On T8 it clicked for credits four times instead of contesting Server 2, and the Corp scored its second Transport Monopoly on T9.
The game was very short: a sensible ice-everything T1 and a Saisentan rez on T2 that flatlined a Runner holding few cards. There is little to judge.

HQ had no ice until T4, so Longevity Serum was stolen from open HQ on T2. Otherwise this was solid Jinteki play: See How They Run scored T3, Urtica Cipher traps in remotes (T5, T10) and an Anemone rez for the flatline on T10.

HQ was left unprotected on T1 (Post-Truth Dividend stolen), and Embedded Reporting in Server 3 behind a single Ping was stolen on T4. Scoring Next Big Thing and Embedded Reporting afterwards was fine, but the double Oppo Research on T12 (4 tags, 7 credits) had no follow-up that used the tags.

Pounding R&D through Hammer and HQ through Ballista won the game, but it had no economy: it stayed at 0-3 credits all game and spent much of its credits clearing Hammer tags. It facechecked remotes with 0-3 credits (Server 1 on T6, Server 2 on T9, Server 3 on T11) and bounced off Descent and Akhet.

Tomorrow's Headline went into a barely-iced Server 2 on T7 with the Corp at 0 credits and was stolen at once, and Embedded Reporting sat unadvanced in Server 1 from T6 until it was stolen on T10. For long stretches (T9-T12, T15-T17, T21-T25) it only clicked for credits while discarding from a full hand every turn, so the game dragged to T27.

It made 12 repeated HQ runs on T11-T13, seeing the same Mindscaping and Neurospike, while ignoring the Server 1 install that scored as Regenesis on T13. On T15-T20 it repeatedly passed Anemone or Karuna on Server 2, then jacked out without accessing, taking net damage for nothing. On T22 it drew four cards instead of running the advanced Server 2 card, which became Longevity Serum.

Setup on T1 was reasonable (Sure Gamble, Shibboleth, Tremolo). On T2 it facechecked the unrezzed Server 1 ice with a 4-card grip and a weak credit pool, and Saisentan flatlined it; that was a risky but not crazy line.

On T1 Drafter installed Project Ingatan into a naked new remote mid-run, and the Runner stole it at once. R&D sat behind a single Wave, which gave up Megaprix Qualifier and Superconducting Hub on T4. Later it hoarded 20-31 credits, clicking for credits on T12-T13 instead of adding ice, though remote scoring eventually won.

Efficient and aggressive: it used Banner to get past Envelopment and Akhet, stole Transport Monopoly twice and SDS Drone Deployment (trashing Buzzsaw to steal), and won on T6. It knowingly sat on 4 cards with Measured Response seen in HQ (T4) and lost its whole grip on T5, which was a risk but not fatal.

The remote scoring was fine (Project Yagi-Uda T4, Hybrid Release T7, Sericulture T9, Yagi-Uda T13). R&D stayed behind a single Hafrun and gave up Fujii Asset Retrieval (T4) and Sericulture (T5), and on T5-T6 it clicked for credits six times instead of adding R&D ice.

Solid tempo: Melies scored T4 off Seamless Launch behind Hagen, and Petty Cash plus Hedge Fund rebuilt credits on T5. Later, layered Ansel, Hagen and Vertigo shut the Runner out. R&D had only one unrezzed ice early (Megaprix stolen T4), and T6-T9 were somewhat passive credit clicks.

After the T4 Into the Depths steal it clicked for credits nearly every turn from T6 to T19, reaching 59 credits, and made almost no runs. Artificial Cryptocrash (T16), Kingmaking (T18) and Remastered Edition (T20) were scored unopposed out of Server 3 after one failed Klevetnik facecheck on T15.
